cohort: 109 women (163 pregnancies) with a history of uterine septum who reached at least 20 weeks gestation
finding: In nulliparous women with viable pregnancies, hysteroscopic resection of a uterine septum is associated with a decreased incidence of preterm birth and an increased incidence of cesarean delivery.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery rates were higher in the resected septum group.
